convoLines.text: "When's the last time you really laughed? Not that it matters."
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it."
"Three days ago. Someone dropped a whole basket of tubers and we just stood there laughing. It wasn't even funny. It was the standing there."
"Still on the last time you laughed."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"The whole fire was arguing about Hummice last night — what to even CALL it. 'Don't-Look' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
You show them Chickweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«Что это за место? Где мы?»
«Да, да, точно.» — Dmitri translates: "Yes, yes, exactly." They nod back, slowly.
«Ты хороший человек.» — Dmitri translates: "You're a good person." A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Я не забуду.» — Dmitri translates: "I won't forget." You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
Their gestures slow — the conversation thinning like light at dusk.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Um — We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"Nobody says Jose's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"What? Teach me something. Anything you know that I don't."
"All right. Show me when we work together."
"Look. I'd like to learn something I can use today. Show me while you work, when you have a moment."
"Still on teaching them something…"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Since Jose died... I keep expecting to see Jose at the fire. Stupid."
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I froze when it mattered. I think about it every day."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Duel. They just... took Sam. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'They fill the quiet. Anyway — where was I?'"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Benoit doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"I count portions out loud before eating. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I'm practicing what I would say if I ever saw my family again. I haven't told anyone."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Halfway to the cache spot, Emilio freezes. Fresh tracks — big. "We go back now. Quietly." You do. The wild, reminding you.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on their secret."
"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
You show them Chickweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"That night — I met The Landlord at the treeline and barely walked away. I keep hearing it when I try to sleep."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one. I mean it."

"It's my grandfather, Ciro. Went in the Taking. He survived two wars and a famine. Not interesting enough, apparently. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
Guadalupe won't meet your eyes. "I told myself finders keepers. It wasn't finders keepers. I'm sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"Still on what was on their mind. Told you."
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"The pantry's nearly bare. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the creek bend, past the treeline."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. I know the creek bend, past the treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took Dmitri — The Blood Tithe, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Same as always: we endure."
"I do the small things right. The big things notice."
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"Still nothing on Ciro. I told you about the pods -- I keep thinking about them. The humming. Some nights I'm sure it's a dream. Other nights I'm sure it's not."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Watch for this: The grass stops moving the way wind moves it. Sweeps Week, every time. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"The Blood Tithe. They just... took Dmitri. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I wake before anyone else. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"Still on what's been happening. That is all."
You show them Chickweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what was on their mind."
"This was good." They mean it.

deathBeat: d9: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Jose Rinaldi is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d9: 🕯️ Jose Rinaldi is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d10: That night, they bring Jose home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d9: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d9: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."
d9: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 35. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 3."
d9: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
d10: ◈ SYSTEM: "Ooh. NEIGHBORS. You know what neighbors are for? STORYLINES. Go knock — worst case, it's CONTENT. Best case? The show gets BIGGER."
d11: SYSTEM: Quest protocol integrated. Objectives will appear.
burialWindowSay: d10: That night, they bring Jose home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d11: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+6 integration)
d12: You say a few words for Jose. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d12: Burying the bloating dead was honest work, and it cost you. Fever by nightfall. (-10 health)
d12: You bury Jose. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)

echoSample: d16: "Nobody says Jose's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
d16: "Since Jose died... I keep expecting to see Jose at the fire. Stupid."
